what_happened: Research for task 683 found that ~/.sapience/config.json's legacy top-level 'folders' list is a hard upstream gate on extract_local.py/upload.py's session-file discovery (_session_candidates: 'f.parent.name in chosen' when non-empty; sync() bails outright when folders==[]), completely independent of capture.projects[].enabled. The vendor CLI 'sapience projects on|off <path>' (upload.py's projects_cli, via _sc.set_project/_persist_capture) touches ONLY capture.projects[], never 'folders' -- confirmed by reading every write site to the folders key, all gated to the interactive onboarding chooser or --reset. So enabling a brand-new repo via the planned hook coupling will show it as enabled in 'sapience projects' but its transcripts will still never be scanned until 'folders' is separately grown, and there is no non-interactive vendor-CLI path to grow it (the onboarding flow refuses outright for a no-TTY invocation without SAPIENCE_ALLOW_ONBOARD=1, and that env var's path is documented as overwriting the ENTIRE saved folder choice, not additive -- unsafe for a per-session hook).

projects_cli (upload.py) has no interactive prompts and unconditionally calls capture_sync() at the end, which itself is a no-op (returns immediately, no network) when TOKEN is unset OR when env SAPIENCE_NO_CAPTURE_SYNC=1 is set. So the hook can invoke 'sapience projects on|off <path>' with SAPIENCE_NO_CAPTURE_SYNC=1 in its environment to get a fully network-free, prompt-free, bounded call -- removing the session-start-hang risk the dispatch flagged, without needing to parse or suppress capture_sync's two bounded (timeout=8) HTTP round-trips at all.
